stage: bounded descriptive continuation research; no strategy selection or execution backtest
user_request: Research whether an opening stretch distance makes further one-direction continuation more likely than retracement.
previous_results_already_known: The unconditional first-touch continuation study and prior fade failures are known and remain preserved. This is a user-requested contextual extension, not a fresh unseen experiment.
entry_unchanged: First touch of plus/minus40,60,80 points from09:30 cash open during09:30 inclusive..09:45 exclusive. No close confirmation, pullback wait or new entry threshold. First-side ambiguity preserved.
hypothesis: Fixed point stretches may have different continuation associations depending on time to first touch and size relative to the opening range typical of the preceding20 eligible sessions.

primary.continuation: Travel another20 points in the initial direction before retracing20 points

supplemental.interpretation: AnotherD in initial direction before a fullD retracement to the open. Supplemental only; cannot rescue primary failure.

hit_time.causality: Minute containing the first touch. This is available at the touch; no future candle close or end-of-minute volume is required. Exact seconds remain unknown.

relative_stretch.scale: Median of the first15-minute high-low range over the previous20 eligible cash sessions, excluding the current day; minimum20 observations; chronological rolling median.shift(1). All cash dates included whether or not they trigger.
relative_stretch.causality: Known before09:30. Never use the current day's completed15-minute range to classify its intrabar entry. First20 cash sessions missing the baseline are recorded explicitly and excluded only from this context family.

bounded_scope: Three triggers x two context families x three bins =18 primary cells per chronological period. Test families separately: no intersections, automatic best-level choice, new bins, refined cutoffs, indicators or further searches after failure.
prior_exposure: All periods already appeared in descriptive research; the chronological check is not a globally unseen holdout or prospective observation.
summaries: Retain all cells including empty/sparse/failed cells. Report n, certain/possible continuation, certain/possible retracement, unresolved/order ambiguity, first-direction ambiguity, mean/median ratio and reference range, and descriptive terminal direction separately if included. Show outcome-ambiguity percentage in every context cell; changing resolution is not automatically a behavioral change.
baseline: For each trigger/period/horizon/barrier/context family, use all threshold-hit events with that family's covariate available. Relative-stretch baseline excludes only its initial20-session warmup. Do not condition on outcome certainty, winners or price reaching any future level.

uncertainty.method: Calendar-month cluster bootstrap including zero-event months throughout each period. Reuse shared sampled month multiplicities across bins and baselines within each period; seeded20261028;20000draws.
uncertainty.pointwise: 95% percentile intervals for certain and possible continuation rates; do not confuse statistical intervals with minute-order bounds.
uncertainty.multiplicity: One-sided lower bound at alpha=0.05/18 for each primary cell's CERTAIN-continuation rate. This conservative Bonferroni bound accounts for18 contextual comparisons. Both chronological periods must pass, rather than cherry-picking one.
uncertainty.continuation_majority_flag: For primary60m20/20 only: at least100 events and12 occupied months in EACH period AND each multiplicity-adjusted lower bound for certain continuation exceeds50%. Otherwise no supported contextual continuation-majority finding.
uncertainty.improvement: Any comparison to an unfiltered cohort is descriptive; overlapping cohorts and partial identification prevent an automatic causal uplift claim. Do not rank or select using upper possible-continuation bounds.
uncertainty.empty_bootstraps: Record count; suppress intervals if fewer than99% of draws have nonzero denominator.

sample_limitations: Inherits1841 complete cash-session sample; three March2020 disruption dates excluded for missing minutes. No forward filling. This may understate halt-related tail risk. Contract rolls, varying index level, price volatility and missing trade sequence limit transfer.
interpretation: No average continuation threshold is defined by overlapping fixed observation levels. A larger average opening range is not a predicted one-direction move. The rolling range is a candidate normalization, not a validated signal.
verification: Validate source hashes; reproduce prior unfiltered event aggregates; check each threshold/date/horizon/barrier event unique; exact bucket boundaries; first20-session warmup and no-lookahead with sentinel perturbation; sums of context bins equal available baseline; joint/known/ambiguous outcome identity; direct independent roll calculation and selected cell reconciliation.
data_acquisition: No paid downloads or external market-data retrievals. Existing local records only, plus read-only published literature research.

fixed_context_contrasts.scope: Each of40/60/80 points separately; primary60m20/20 only; development and chronological-check periods separately. Six fixed contrasts per period; no fitted or chosen contrasts.
fixed_context_contrasts.identification_bounds: [certain_A - possible_B, possible_A - certain_B], in percentage points; preserve paired month resampling.
fixed_context_contrasts.intervals: Pointwise95% percentile intervals for each identification endpoint, only if both groups meet100events and12occupiedmonths and99% valid bootstrap draws.
fixed_context_contrasts.interpretation: Descriptive associations with no formal contrast-selection flag; no causal effect or executable profit claim. Report all six pairs even if sparse or crossing zero.
